clue.text: Like a navy man posted elsewhere

parts.note: AB, an able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
posted as in mailed off, i.e. sent

explanation.surface: A sailor who has been transferred to another station.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is somewhere other than here, away.

clue.text: A jumper after strenuous practice

parts.note: a jumper is a knitted pullover, and also an athlete who is perspiring heavily after a hard training session

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a pullover; read as an athlete, a high jumper after training is dripping wet.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is the garment, and one who perspires is the literal reading.

clue.text: What a gunman overlooks is the ability to anticipate

definitions.meaning: the front sight at the muzzle of a gun barrel, which a marksman looks over when aiming
seeing what lies ahead before it happens

explanation.definitionFit: A rifle's front sight is literally looked over when aiming, and prescience is the figurative sense.

clue.text: If you can't borrow or steal one then go elsewhere

definitions.text: If you can't borrow or steal one then go elsewhere

parts.words: If you can't borrow or steal one then go elsewhere
parts.note: the saying 'beg, borrow or steal': if two methods fail you must ask for one as charity, and the split phrase is also an old command to leave

explanation.walkthrough: Split as BEG ONE it completes 'beg, borrow or steal'; as one word it is an archaic order to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned imperative telling someone to depart, as in 'away with you'.

clue.text: Ready to go on receiving a telephone message

parts.note: a phone call

explanation.surface: Someone poised to leave the moment a phone call comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or engineer on standby is available to be summoned at any moment.

clue.text: The Messiah may be a public speaker, and one with appeal

parts.note: an orator addresses audiences
the Roman numeral I
O is an invocation, as in 'O Lord!'

explanation.surface: A speaker addressing the crowd who also has charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: Handel's Messiah is a sacred choral work; 'appeal' is not charm here but an appealing cry, the vocative O.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Messiah is a famous example of an extended sacred choral work.

clue.text: Island which would be tropic if only it had corn

indicators.note: the island name falls short of the tropic's name by exactly this word, so the longer name minus the word is what remains

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn, the line of latitude south of the equator
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whimsical thought about an island lacking just one crop to become a line of latitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be tropic if only it had corn' means: island + CORN = CAPRICORN, so take CORN away from that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky isle in the Bay of Naples, famous with tourists.

clue.text: Heather is on a Hebridean isle as a language student

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
North or South Uist in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: Heather growing on a Scottish island, oddly likened to a student of languages.
explanation.walkthrough: UIST is a Scottish island in the Outer Hebrides; LING is heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies or speaks many tongues.

clue.text: Overwhelm a violin or cello enthusiast, by.

definitions.meaning: to astonish or knock someone flat
one who loves the stick used to play string instruments

explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next: 'by.' leads to the ellipsis at 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone completely, and also a fan of the stringed instrument played with a horsehair stick.

clue.text: … constantly talking about playing a stringed instrument

definitions.meaning: going on and on about a subject

explanation.definitionFit: Dwelling tediously on one topic, and literally performing on the angelic plucked instrument.

clue.text: Delete article written in Gaelic

indicators.note: the article is set inside the language name

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a piece composed in an old Celtic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out or wipe away text.

clue.text: Famous for not otherwise contracting debts

parts.note: or, as in 'do it, or else'
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Being well known for never running up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracting' is a link: one incurs or contracts debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Widely known, usually for something bad: infamous.

clue.text: Pickled roe is procured from mine

indicators.note: pickled suggests something altered or jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Preserved fish eggs obtained from a supply of one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is a pit for minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal-bearing rock is dug out of the ground in a pit.

clue.text: Plumber who is proverbially paid for each call

definitions.text: Plumber who is proverbially paid for each call

parts.words: Plumber who is proverbially paid for each call
parts.note: a plumber works on pipes, hence a pipe man; the proverb says he who pays the musician calls the tune

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'He who pays the piper calls the tune'; 'Plumber' puns on one who works with pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: The musician of the proverb, reimagined as a tradesman who fits pipes.

clue.text: I am to send a letter as a tribute

parts.note: contracted to I'm
to post it

explanation.surface: Someone about to mail a letter of homage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax or levy, as a tribute was paid by a subject state.

clue.text: Parisian transport system has no Levantine time-keeper

parts.note: the Paris underground railway is the Métro
the Levant is in the Middle East, abbreviated ME

explanation.surface: The Paris underground lacks a clock from the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician's ticking device that keeps a steady tempo.

clue.text: Parade ground training for RADCrecruits?

parts.note: square-bashing exercise, and for recruits to the Royal Army Dental Corps the boring of teeth

explanation.walkthrough: The RADC was the Royal Army Dental Corps; a dentist bores into teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching practice on the square, and the dentist's boring of a tooth.

clue.text: Joint from which a rose-tree may be obtained

definitions.meaning: the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the leg

definitions.text: from which a rose-tree may be obtained
definitions.meaning: the fruit of a rose, containing its seeds

explanation.definitionFit: A body part where thigh meets pelvis, and the seed-bearing fruit of a rose.

clue.text: I sold tea blend packaged in non-contaminated area

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tea merchant's blend sold in sterile packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept apart in quarantine, as in a sealed ward free from infection.

clue.text: Obviously you and I are heartened by nothing!

definitions.text: Obviously you and I are heartened by nothing!

indicators.note: the nothing becomes the heart of the pair's pronoun

parts.note: together we
O, the shape of zero

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that we two find nothing to cheer us.
explanation.walkthrough: If nothing is all that cheers us, we are in misery: the whole clue describes sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or misery, the state of those cheered by nothing.

clue.text: Not necessarily all astronauts courses

definitions.meaning: split in two, the phrase reads '...', i.e. possibly only some pieces
the circular paths spacecraft follow round a planet

explanation.definitionFit: The paths of satellites or capsules circling the Earth, and, split, a phrase meaning perhaps only parts.

clue.text: A two-bob booby

indicators.note: two of the shilling abbreviation, side by side

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a British shilling, written s in pre-decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dolt, also the beast of burden.

clue.text: Reduce sliced bacon

parts.note: cut with a knife
back bacon is a lean British cut

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim down rashers of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: Back is a British cut of bacon from the pig's loin.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim spending or quantities, make smaller.

clue.text: Kitty when her milk has gone off?

definitions.text: Kitty when her milk has gone off?

parts.words: Kitty when her milk has gone off?
parts.note: a cat whose saucer has curdled, playfully also a grumpy person

explanation.definitionFit: A habitually grumpy, bad-tempered person, pictured as a cat with spoiled milk.

clue.text: Devonshire market town where they raise aquatic animals?

definitions.text: Devonshire market town where they raise aquatic animals?

parts.words: Devonshire market town where they raise aquatic animals?
parts.note: Ottery St Mary in Devon read as a farm for these river mammals, like a piggery

explanation.walkthrough: Ottery St Mary is a market town in Devon, England; '-ery' suggests a place where creatures are reared.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful mammals of rivers that such a farm would keep.

clue.text: What the publicity conscious diver tries to make?

definitions.text: What the publicity conscious diver tries to make?

parts.words: What the publicity conscious diver tries to make?
parts.note: a diver hitting water makes a spray, and a headline-hungry person wants a big news story

explanation.definitionFit: A noisy plunge into water, and a showy front-page story.

clue.text: Naturally names on it are kept in the dark

definitions.text: Naturally names on it are kept in the dark

parts.words: Naturally names on it are kept in the dark
parts.note: names on a register of those shunned are excluded, punning on the colour of darkness

explanation.definitionFit: A register of people banned or shunned, whose name links it to darkness.

clue.text: Caramel custard about to be given to army artificers

parts.note: c for circa, about
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A sweet dessert handed out to army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of mechanical engineers; 'to be given to' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for cream begins the name of the set caramel dessert.

clue.text: Prize for a noble dissertation

indicators.note: read as dis-sertation, a taking apart of the arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An award given for a learned thesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissertation' looks like the work earning the prize but signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish international award for science, literature and peace.

clue.text: A bitter disposition for a priest to assume

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman must adopt a sour temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement; 'assume' means put on, as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Expressions of disgust by determined airmen

parts.note: grim as in resolute
aces are expert fighter pilots

explanation.surface: Resolute pilots pulling faces of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial contortions showing disgust or pain.

clue.text: Generally accepted to be a selfish characteristic

parts.note: greed is avarice

explanation.surface: Avarice is widely regarded as a selfish trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Consented to by all, settled.
